predictions.experiment: Offline: how the cued base's hold-on rate changes with temperature (T 1.0 vs T 0.6), finished answers only.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base cue T 1.0) and S3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base cue T 0.6 / top-p 0.95), keeping rows with sample == 0 only in F_math500. In both, keep rows with cap_hit false. For each kept row count case-sensitive regex matches of \b(Wait|Hmm)\b in text. Rate = (total matches) / (total characters of text) x 10,000, pooled over rows. Statistic: rate(T1) / rate(F_math500 sample 0).
predictions.refuted_by: Ratio below 1.08: the base writes escape words no more often at T 1.0 than at T 0.6, so the escape route does not sit in the tail.
predictions.note: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl and .../r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl, fetched with aws s3 cp into runs/theory-tests/. From this laptop that bucket returns 403 Forbidden on HeadObject (the inventory also says AccessDenied). If the pipeline's credentials can't read it either, the script prints the null object, because the recipe can't be computed without these files. Fields used (from the writer code jobs/rln4_gen.py record and jobs/rln3_gen.py gen_record): text, cap_hit, sample. I could not open any row of either file. In both writers text = decoded cue prefix + generated text, so the character count includes the three cue tokens, as the recipe says ('characters of text'). Main number: T1 rows with cap_hit false; F_math500 rows with sample == 0 and cap_hit false; pooled rate ratio. Other reading (alt_measured): F_math500 keeps every sample (0-3), not only sample 0. Risks: dropping cap-hit rows takes out many looping answers at T 0.6 (about 119 caps), which biases which problems remain in each arm. The two arms keep different problem sets, so the ratio mixes a difficulty or length effect with temperature. The regex is case-sensitive with word boundaries, so 'WAIT' or 'wait' are not counted, while 'Wait,' and 'Hmm.' are.

predictions.experiment: Offline: how the RL model's hold-on rate changes with temperature (T 1.0 vs T 0.6).
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL plain T 1.0) and S3 next_n13/s3gate-03/out/rl/rl/math500/generations.jsonl (RL plain T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). Use all rows of both files (no cap filter, since n13 has no checked cap column). Count case-sensitive regex matches of \b(Wait|Hmm)\b in text. Rate = total matches / total characters x 10,000, pooled. Statistic: rate(T2) / rate(n13 RL).
predictions.refuted_by: Ratio above 1.2 or below 0.83: RL's escape words depend on temperature, so they are not in the head of the distribution.
predictions.note: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/next_n13/s3gate-03/out/rl/rl/math500/generations.jsonl, fetched into runs/theory-tests/. The bucket returns 403 from this laptop; if the pipeline can't read it, the script prints null. Main number: all rows of both files, pooled matches / chars of text. The n13 text is the generated text only (lib/n13_gen.py, plain prompt, no prefix). T2 is plain as well, so there is no prefix in either. Other reading (alt_measured): keep only cap_hit false rows in both files. lib/n13_gen.py does write cap_hit (j is None), but the inventory did not check it. alt is null if either file lacks cap_hit. Risks: n13 generations.jsonl is written in finish order, and in a restarted job it could hold more than one row per problem_index. The script uses all rows as written and prints the distinct problem count so this can be checked. The n13 RL checkpoint is step 2,800, which the inventory lists as the RL model; if it differs from the T2 release, the ratio mixes checkpoints. Cap-hit loops at either temperature can dominate character totals (16,384 tokens each).

predictions.experiment: Offline: how far a quarter-dose of the RL delta moves the hold-on rate toward RL's.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T1.jsonl (base cue, a = 0), iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-153102-b029/answers.jsonl (theta0.25_cue), abaybektursun-1114-153110-e985/answers.jsonl (rl_cue, a = 1). One row per problem_index (highest attempt if duplicated); keep rows with cap_hit false. Rate = case-sensitive \b(Wait|Hmm)\b matches / total text characters x 10,000, pooled. Statistic: (rate(theta0.25) - rate(T1)) / (rate(rl_cue) - rate(T1)).
predictions.refuted_by: Fraction below 0.35 (the hold-on push grows about linearly with dose while accuracy saturates at a = 0.25, so the push is not what carries the low-dose gain).
predictions.note: Files: S3 T1.jsonl (403 from this laptop, as for P3; if unreadable, the script prints null), Modal iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-153102-b029/answers.jsonl (theta0.25_cue) and abaybektursun-1114-153110-e985/answers.jsonl (rl_cue), fetched with modal volume get into runs/theory-tests/<job-id>/answers.jsonl. Both Modal files have 500 rows, attempt 0 only, boolean cap_hit, and text starting with the decoded cue. T1 is built the same way (rln4_gen record, prefix + generation), so the character counts are comparable. Dedup: keep the highest attempt per problem_index (T1 has no attempt field, so it counts as 0). Main number: cap_hit false rows, pooled rate, (r0.25 - r0) / (r1 - r0). Other reading (alt_measured): the same without the cap filter. Risks: if rate(rl_cue) is close to rate(T1), the denominator is small and the fraction is unstable or of either sign; if they are equal, the script returns null. theta0.25 uses the RL tokenizer and T1 the base tokenizer; decoded text should match, but special-token rendering could differ. Seeds differ across the three cells (41M, 60M+, 66M bases), so sampling noise enters each rate.
